summary: Nine machines are scheduled for repair over the next 14 days, with a total expected cost of $106,539. Three machines (2, 3, 8) have no repair planned because their forecasted days left are long and failure risk is low. Repairs are scheduled on days with available technicians, avoiding days 5, 6, 12, 13, 19, and 20. All planned repairs occur on days with normal production and one technician assigned. The plan prioritizes machines with high sensor wear or short time before failure, such as machine 7 which has a 51% chance of failing before repair.

reasons.0: Scheduled on day 2 because it has 100% sensor wear and a 10% chance of failing before repair, with a likely failure in 4 days.
reasons.1: Scheduled on day 3 due to 62% sensor wear and a forecasted likely failure in 11 days, allowing early repair.
reasons.4: Scheduled on day 9 because it has 100% sensor wear and a likely failure in 15 days, fitting the available technician schedule.
reasons.5: Scheduled on day 14 due to 64% sensor wear and a likely failure in 21 days, with no technicians available before that.
reasons.6: Scheduled on day 11 because it has 100% sensor wear and a likely failure in 24 days, aligning with technician availability.
reasons.7: Scheduled on day 10 due to a 51% chance of failing before repair and 83% sensor wear, making it the highest priority.
reasons.9: Scheduled on day 4 because it has 88% sensor wear and a likely failure in 12 days, with day 4 available.
reasons.10: Scheduled on day 1 due to 93% sensor wear and a likely failure in 2 days, requiring immediate repair.
reasons.11: Scheduled on day 0 because it has 100% sensor wear and a likely failure in 4 days, so it is repaired today.
